html:
The Velvet Revolution was the peaceful overthrow of communist rule in Czechoslovakia between 17 November and 29 December 1989, set off when riot police beat students at a march in Prague.

The march, marking the Nazi closing of Czech universities in 1939, was attacked on Národní Street. Students and theatres went on strike, and huge crowds filled Wenceslas Square, jingling keys. The dissident playwright Václav Havel led the Civic Forum, and a general strike on 27 November showed that the whole country supported change. The Communist Party gave up its leading role. On 29 December parliament elected Havel president, with Dubček as its speaker. Free elections followed in 1990. It was part of the revolutions of 1989, and three years later came the split with Slovakia.
sum: The Velvet Revolution was the peaceful overthrow of communist rule in Czechoslovakia between 17 November and 29 December 1989, set off when riot police beat students at a march in Prague.
